script: Everyone thinks Vikings wore horned helmets, they never did. Real Viking-era helmets that archaeologists have found are plain, rounded, and built purely for protection in battle. The horned image came from an opera costume designer in the 1870s, working on a production about Norse gods centuries after the Viking age ended. He wanted something dramatic on stage, and horns looked striking under theater lights. Audiences loved the image, and it spread through paintings, illustrations, and eventually textbooks that never bothered to check archaeology. Real warriors never fought wearing horns bolted to their heads, useless weight that an enemy could grab in close combat. But the costume version was more exciting than the truth, so historians kept losing that fight for over a century. Everyone still thinks Vikings wore horned helmets, and an opera costume designer is the reason why.
